title: Fix leftover configure placeholders in cutlass/version.h
body:
Fixes #3472

`getVersionString()` and `getGitRevision()` in `include/cutlass/version.h` returned the literal strings `@CUTLASS_VERSION@` and `@CUTLASS_REVISION@`. Those were left behind when the `configure_file` step for `version.h` was dropped in 3.4.1 (bbe579a); only `cmake/version_extended.h.in` is generated, so nothing ever substituted them, and even a full CMake build prints `CUTLASS @CUTLASS_VERSION@` in the profiler banner (`tools/profiler/src/options.cu`).

This builds `getVersionString()` from the CUTLASS_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH macros and lets `getGitRevision()` return CUTLASS_REVISION, which is empty by default and supplied by `version_extended.h` under `CUTLASS_VERSIONS_GENERATED`. The build-number suffix behavior is unchanged.

Behavior note: the profiler banner changes from `CUTLASS @CUTLASS_VERSION@ ... commit @CUTLASS_REVISION@` to `CUTLASS 4.7.0`, with the commit clause printed only when a real revision exists. Nothing in-tree parses the old string.

Adds `test/unit/core/version.cu` (3 tests) registered in `test/unit/core/CMakeLists.txt`.

Test Plan:
```
$ docker run --rm -v .../cutlass:/src:ro nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 \
    g++ -std=c++17 -I/src/include host_check.cpp && ./host_check
  unfixed header: getVersionString=@CUTLASS_VERSION@
                  getGitRevision=@CUTLASS_REVISION@   -> 4 assertion failures
  fixed header:   getVersionString=4.7.0 getGitRevision=    -> 0 failures

$ docker run --rm nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04   # nvcc V12.8.93 + googletest
$ nvcc -std=c++17 -I<include> -I<gtest include> -c test/unit/core/version.cu ...
$ g++ version.o libgtest.a libgtest_main.a -lcudart -o vt && ./vt
[==========] 3 tests from 1 test suite ran. (1 ms total)
[  PASSED  ] 3 tests.
```
Both configurations were also compiled with MSVC against a simulated generated `version_extended.h`: defaults give `"4.7.0"`/`""`, generated gives `"4.7.0.5"`/`"abc123"`.

title: Skip stale entries in the DSL shared library list
body:
Fixes #3462 (part 2: worker-side hard failure)

`get_shared_libs` raised `FileNotFoundError` on the first missing entry of the colon-separated `{prefix}_LIBS` list. The list travels inside job environments (Slurm `sbatch` defaults to `--export=ALL`), so a worker can receive an entry pointing into the submitter's site-packages, and every compile died on it even though another entry named a usable local runtime.

This skips entries whose file does not exist on this machine and warns about them instead. It keeps raising when nothing in the list survives, since that means there is no usable runtime at all and the compile cannot proceed.

Part 1 of the issue (the import-time `CUTE_DSL_LIBS` mutation that manufactures these stale entries) is a separate mechanism in a separate file and is intentionally not bundled here.

Adds `test/python/CuTeDSL/test_shared_libs.py` (3 CPU-only tests using a stubbed DSL instance).

Test Plan:
```
$ docker run --rm python:3.12-slim ...   # editable install of python/CuTeDSL
$ CUTE_DSL_LIBS=/nonexistent/libcute_dsl_runtime.so:<valid cu12/lib/libcute_dsl_runtime.so> \
    python -c "<compile a trivial @cute.jit function>"
  unfixed: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
           '/nonexistent/libcute_dsl_runtime.so'
  fixed:   UserWarning: Skipping /nonexistent/libcute_dsl_runtime.so ... other
           entries ... point at a usable runtime.
           COMPILE_OK

$ CUTE_DSL_LIBS=/nonexistent/a.so:/nonexistent/b.so ...
  fixed:   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
           '/nonexistent/a.so:/nonexistent/b.so'

$ python test/python/CuTeDSL/test_shared_libs.py -v
  Ran 3 tests ... OK   (the mixed-entry test fails on unfixed code)
```

Known same-class gaps left out of scope: `cutlass/jax/ffi.py::find_cute_dsl_runtime_library` and `tvm_ffi_provider.py` still return the first name-matching entry without an existence check.

title: Update 4.8 tag
update 4.8 release
[CuTeDSL] Fix CLC epilogue TMA-store stage rotation
body:
## Summary

- Track completed CLC work tiles locally in the epilogue warps.
- Rotate TMA-store shared-memory stages using the epilogue's actual tile count.
- Prevent short-K dynamic persistent GEMMs from reusing an SMEM stage while its previous TMA store is still in flight.

## Root cause

`ClcDynamicPersistentTileScheduler` is instantiated independently in each specialized warp. Only the scheduler warp calls `advance_to_next_work()`, which increments that instance's `num_tiles_executed`. The TMA, MMA, and epilogue warps consume the CLC response through `get_current_work()`, so their scheduler-local counters remain zero.

The TMA-store epilogue uses `num_tiles_executed` to select its C-SMEM stage:

```text
c_buffer =
    (num_tiles_executed * subtile_count + subtile_idx)
    % num_c_stages
```

For the reproducer below, each M64xN256 output tile has four M64xN64 epilogue subtiles and a three-stage C-SMEM ring. A counter permanently equal to zero restarts every output tile at stage zero and can overwrite a stage still owned by an earlier asynchronous TMA store. Large K hides the race behind mainloop latency; short K exposes it.

## Fix

Initialize a local epilogue tile counter before the persistent loop and increment it after each completed tile. This keeps all epilogue threads in lockstep and avoids changing the public CLC scheduler semantics.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- GPU: NVIDIA B30Z, compute capability 10.3
- A/B/C: FP16/FP16/FP16, FP32 accumulation
- CTA tile: M64xN256
- CTA group: 1
- Cluster: `(1,1)`
- CLC raster/swizzle: M/1
- TMA store: enabled

Before this change:

```text
MNK: 8256x8448x128
Mismatched elements: 755401 / 69746688 (1.1%)
Greatest absolute difference: 158.0
```

After this change:

```text
MNK: 8256x8448x128
FP32 reference check: PASS
```

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile .../dense_gemm_persistent_dynamic.py`: PASS
- FP16 `8256x8448x128`, CTA M64xN256, cluster `(1,1)`, TMA store: PASS
- FP16 `8192x8192x8192`, CTA M64xN256, cluster `(1,1)`, TMA store: PASS
  - Smoke runtime: 976.69 us
- FP16 `4096x4096x128`, CTA M64xN256, cluster `(1,2)`, TMA multicast + TMA store: PASS
- FP16 `4096x4096x128`, CTA M64xN256, cluster `(1,1)`, direct non-TMA epilogue: PASS

The full-K target remains performance-neutral; this change only corrects C-SMEM ring indexing in fast tile-turnover cases.

## Scope

This PR intentionally does not change CLC swizzle-domain padding behavior. That is a separate issue and should be handled independently.

title: [CuTeDSL] Use vectorized codegen for CUDA 12.9 2CTA grouped GEMM
body:
The contiguous grouped GEMM example currently selects scalar RMEM operations and O3 for all CUDA 12.9 configurations. Enable vectorized RMEM/O2 for 2CTA while retaining scalar RMEM/O3 for 1CTA. The same predicate continues to select both the RMEM implementation and compilation options; CUDA 13.1+ retains its existing selection.

Validation used the public `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.8.0.dev0` wheel (CUDA 12.9 backend) on GB200 at 802 MHz. With M=1024, N=4096, L=16, FP8 E4M3 inputs, BF16 output, a 128x128 MMA tile, fixed M and cold L2:

| Case | Before (us) | After (us) | Latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1CTA, K1024, cluster 1x1 | 27.965 | 27.998 | 0.12% |
| 2CTA, K4096, cluster 2x1 | 100.596 | 90.523 | -10.01% |

Measurements were interleaved A/B/B/A, with 20 warmups, 100 iterations per trial and five trials per process. Each table entry averages the two process medians. The 1CTA kernel cubins are byte-identical.

Ten local reference checks passed: both CTA modes at K1024/K4096, irregular M/N/K and both C-major layouts, plus the baseline controls. Ruff formatting, DSL example lint checks and `git diff --check` passed. This PR changes only the example kernel.

title: Add opt-in persistent caching to cute.compile
body:
## Summary

- add `use_cache=True` to `cute.compile` to reuse the existing invalidating in-memory and file cache
- preserve the current uncached default for backward compatibility and custom executor caches
- keep `CUTE_DSL_NO_CACHE` and PTX/CUBIN/SASS dump behavior authoritative
- document that frontend tracing still runs to validate the cache key

## Testing

- focused test: `6 passed`
- Python compile check for modified files
- CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0 on NVIDIA B300 with CUDA 13.2
- fresh-process file-cache hit with backend compilation replaced by an exception
- compiled executor launch and output verification on both the original and changed captured constant
- default path confirmed to write no cache entries
- `git diff --check`

title: [CuTeDSL] Guard SM100 UMMA peer arrival mask on the cluster v-extent
body:
**Fixes #3658.** Verified on hardware: the reported fault reproduces before this change and is gone after.

## Cause

`_compute_mcast_arrival_mask` unconditionally ORs in image masks taken at the v-peer coordinate `(v ^ 1, m, n, k)`. That peer only exists for a 2CTA tcgen05 MMA (v-extent 2). At v-extent 1 the coordinate is outside the layout's domain, and if mode 0 carries a non-zero stride the peer image runs off the end of the cluster — `(1,4,1,1):(1,1,4,4)` yields mask `0b11111`, setting bit 4 of a 4-CTA cluster. The mask feeds `tcgen05.commit(..., multicast::cluster)`, so that is an out-of-range remote mbarrier access.

## Fix

Compute the peer terms only when the v-extent is not 1 — the same guard `PipelineAsyncUmma.create` already applies, and the semantics of the C++ `detail::calculate_multicast_mask`, which never addresses a rank outside the cluster.

## Verification

GB300 (`sm_103a`), CUDA 13.0, DSL 4.8.0 — 4-CTA cluster through `PipelineTmaUmma.consumer_release`:

| `cta_layout_vmnk` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `(1,4,1,1):(1,1,4,4)` 1SM | **`cudaErrorLaunchFailure` (719)** | `cudaSuccess` |
| `(1,4,1,1):(0,1,0,0)` 1SM | `cudaSuccess` | `cudaSuccess` |
| `((2),2,1,1):((1),2,0,0)` 2SM | `cudaSuccess` | `cudaSuccess` |
| `((2),1,2,1):((1),0,2,0)` 2SM | `cudaSuccess` | `cudaSuccess` |

No in-tree caller is affected — `make_layout`, `tiled_divide` and `make_ordered_layout` give extent-1 modes stride 0, which makes the peer terms inert. `dense_gemm.py` is identical before and after for cluster shapes 1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, 4x1, 1x4 and 4x4 in both 1SM and 2CTA modes.

title: [CuTe] Mask ThrK in TiledMMA::get_layoutC_TV (#3612)
body:
## Motivation

#3612: `TiledMMA::get_layoutC_TV()` disagrees with `ThrMMA::partition_C()` when the TiledMMA's thread layout has a K mode (`ThrK > 1`). The disagreement goes beyond wrong offsets: the returned layout maps threads **outside the C tile**. With the issue's example (`UniversalFMA`, thread layout `(2,3,4)`, a 2x3 C tile), `cosize(get_layoutC_TV())` is 24, and 18 of the 24 threads report offsets 6..23.

`get_layoutC_TV()` is also the input of `make_tiled_copy_C` / `make_tiled_copy_C_atom`, so those produce wrong tiled copies for such TiledMMAs as well.

## Root cause

`thrfrg_C` produces a thread mode `(ThrV,(ThrM,ThrN))`, which has no K mode. `get_layoutC_TV()` composes it directly with `thridx_2_thrid`, which maps `thr_idx` to a linear `(ThrV,ThrM,ThrN,ThrK)` index. When `ThrK > 1` that index runs past the thread mode's domain. For threads with K coordinate > 0, the composed layout then either extends beyond the tile or lands on the wrong element.

`get_layoutA_TV()` / `get_layoutB_TV()` avoid this. They first compose their thread mode with a tile that re-inserts the missing thread mode (N for A, M for B) with stride 0 (`atile` / `btile`), so it lines up with `(ThrV,ThrM,ThrN,ThrK)`. `get_layoutC_TV()` has no such step.

## Modifications

- `include/cute/atom/mma_atom.hpp`: add the missing `ctile`, which maps `(ThrV,(ThrM,ThrN))` to `(ThrV,(ThrM,(ThrN,ThrK)))` with stride 0 on `ThrK`, exactly like `atile` / `btile`. Threads that differ only in their K coordinate now map to the same C elements, as in `partition_C()`, which drops `ThrK`.
- New `test/unit/cute/core/tiled_mma.cpp` (host-only, in `cutlass_test_unit_cute_core`). For every thread and every value, it checks that `get_layout{C,A,B}_TV()` match `partition_{C,A,B}()` and stay inside the tile. It covers UniversalFMA with `ThrK` 1/2/4 (including a K-fastest thread order and a permuted tile) and `SM80_16x8x16_F32F16F16F32_TN` with `ThrK` 1/2/4 and permutations.

## Testing

**Correctness for `ThrK > 1`** (host, g++ 13). The check compares `get_layoutC_TV()(t,v)` with `partition_C` for every thread and value:

| TiledMMA | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| UniversalFMA thr (2,3,2) / (2,3,4) | 6 / 18 wrong, all out of tile | 0 |
| UniversalFMA thr (4,4,2) row-major; (2,2,2) K-fastest | 16 / 4 wrong | 0 |
| UniversalFMA thr (4,2,2), perm 16x8x4 | 128 wrong (only 32 out of tile, the other 96 are **silently wrong in-tile**) | 0 |
| SM80 16x8x16 thr (2,2,2) / (1,2,4) / (2,2,2) perm 32x32x32 | 512 / 768 / 1024 wrong | 0 |
| SM80 8x8x4 F64, SM75 16x8x8, SM70 8x8x4, thr (2,2,2) | 256 / 512 / 256 wrong | 0 |

The new unit test fails without the fix (2476 mismatches, 8 layouts reaching outside the tile) and passes with it.

**No change for `ThrK == 1`,** which covers all in-tree uses:
- *Layouts:* I dumped the full mappings of `get_layoutC_TV()`, `make_tiled_copy_C(...)` and `make_tiled_copy_C_atom(...)` (S/D TV layouts and tiler) with and without this change. The configurations were UniversalFMA, SM70/SM75/SM80 atoms with and without permutations, and SM90 GMMA 64x128x16 with 1 and 2 warpgroups, paired with UniversalCopy and `SM90_U32x{2,4}_STSM_N`. Across 14 configurations the 221,615 mapped values are **byte-identical**.
- *SASS:* I compiled four translation units twice, with only `mma_atom.hpp` differing, for `sm_80`, `sm_90a` and `sm_100a` (CUDA 12.8), and compared `cuobjdump -sass`. The dependency files confirm that each build picked up its own header. The SASS is **identical**:

  | translation unit | uses | kernels | SASS instructions |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `sm90_gemm_f16_f16_f16_tensor_op_f32_cluster_warpspecialized_pingpong.cu` | SM90 TMA epilogue, `make_tiled_copy_C` | 84 | 80,016 = 80,016 |
  | `examples/50_hopper_gemm_with_epilogue_swizzle.cu` | SM70/80 vectorized `collective::Epilogue`, `make_tiled_copy_C` | 18 | 18,368 = 18,368 |
  | `test/unit/cute/ampere/cooperative_gemm.cu` | `cooperative_gemm`, `make_tiled_copy_C` | 96 | 61,384 = 61,384 |
  | `sm80_gemm_f16_f16_f32_tensor_op_f32.cu` | SM80 3.x mainloop with `DefaultEpilogue` (TiledMMA partitioning only) | 12 | 27,344 = 27,344 |

  Together these cover every in-tree caller of `make_tiled_copy_C` / `make_tiled_copy_C_atom` (`sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`, `sm70_epilogue_vectorized.hpp`, `cooperative_gemm.hpp`). The `_array` epilogue variants use the same calls.

**Unit tests with this change** (H200):

| target | result |
|---|---|
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_core` (includes the new `tiled_mma.cpp`) | 53 passed |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_ampere` | 228 passed |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_hopper_cooperative_gemm` | 1 passed |

Closes #3612

title: [C++] Fix SM120 blockscaled small-N tiles breaking cutlass_profiler builds (#3646)
body:
## Motivation

#3646: `make cutlass_profiler` fails for `CUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS=120a`:

```
sm90_common.inl(321): error: static assertion failed with "BLK_K0 must be a multiple of size<1>(GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<ElementType>{})"
  ... ss_smem_selector<K, float_e5m2_t, _128, _8> ... sm120_get_epilogue_smem_swizzle_layout_atom ...
  ... cutlass3x_sm120_bstensorop_gemm_ue8m0xe4m3_ue8m0xe2m3_f32_void_e5m2_128x8x128_1x1x1_0_tnt_align128_cooperative_q.cu
```

## Root cause

This is a regression from #3176 ("Small Tile N BlockScaled GEMM"). That PR added N = 8/16/32/64 CTA tiles to `GenerateSM120_TensorOp_mixed_8bits_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled` and `GenerateSM120_TensorOp_fp4_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled`. There are two problems:

1. **The small tiles were put first.** Without a kernel filter, `CreateGemmUniversal3xOperator` instantiates only `tile_descriptions[0]` ("by default, only generate the largest tile"). Before #3176 that was `[128, 128, 128]`. Now it is `[128, 8, 128]` (cooperative) or `[128, 16, 128]` (ping-pong). A default `120a` configure of current `main` emits 286 non-grouped SM120 blockscaled GEMMs: 172 at N=8, 114 at N=16, and **none** at N=128.
2. **Every small tile is combined with every data type,** but for row-major C/D with `EpilogueTileAuto` the collective builders only accept some combinations:
   - **R1:** the epilogue tile N (`min(CTA_N, 32)`, from `sm120_compute_tile_shape_or_override`) must span a multiple of 128 bits for C and D. This comes from the swizzle atom in `ss_smem_selector` (`sm90_common.inl:321`). FP6 is stored in 8-bit containers.
   - **R2:** FP6 D needs `CTA_N % 128 == 0` (`sm120_builder.inl:158`).
   - **R3:** block-scaled D needs epilogue tile N / SFD vector size in {1, 2, 4, 8} (`Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore`, `sm120_visitor_store_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:72`).
   - **R4:** 6-bit B needs `CTA_N >= 32`. `sm120_rr_smem_copy_selector_B` (`sm120_common.inl:81`) always picks `SM100_SU6_DU8x16_x4_LDSM_N` for 6-bit B, so smaller N fails with "TiledCopy uses too few vals for selected CopyAtom". #3176 added x1/x2 variants only for 4-bit and 8-bit B.

**How many kernels fail (CUDA 12.8, `sm_120a`, the 286 kernels of a default build of current `main`):**

| | N=8 | N=16 | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| fail to compile | 155 / 172 | 78 / 114 | **233 / 286** |

The first error in each failed compile:

| error | count | constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `BLK_K0 must be a multiple of size<1>(GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom...)` | 103 | R1 |
| `CTA tile for FP6 ElementD must have a contiguous extent that is a multiple of 128.` | 75 | R2 |
| `TiledCopy uses too few vals for selected CopyAtom` | 30 | R4 |
| `EpilogueTileN should be divisible by SFVecSize` | 25 | R3 |

I spot-checked each error class with CUDA 13.0 and got the same results.

## Modifications

`python/cutlass_library/generator.py`, SM120 blockscaled dense generators only:

- Put the original large tiles back at the front of `tile_sizes_cooperative` / `tile_sizes_pingpong`, followed by the small-N tiles in decreasing N. A default build instantiates `[128, 128, 128]` again, as it did before #3176.
- Add `sm120_blockscaled_supports_tile_n(tile_n, data_type)`, which encodes R1–R4. Each data type is generated only with the tile N values the builders accept, so filtered builds (for example `CUTLASS_LIBRARY_KERNELS=cutlass3x_sm120*`) no longer contain kernels that cannot compile. The small tiles remain wherever they are valid, for example f32/f16 output at N=8, e5m2 output at N=16, and FP4 output at N=32/64.

No C++ changes. The x1/x2 variants of `SM100_SU6_DU8x16_*_LDSM_N` exist, so an alternative for R4 would be to extend `sm120_rr_smem_copy_selector_B` the way #3176 did for 4-bit and 8-bit B. That would add new FP6-B small-tile kernels, and I can't validate them without SM120 hardware, so I left the selector as is.

## Testing

I ran compile-only checks, because I have no SM120 GPU (`-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS=120a`).

**The filter agrees with nvcc on every kernel of the default build.** Of the 286 compile outcomes above, `sm120_blockscaled_supports_tile_n` accepts exactly the 53 that compile and rejects exactly the 233 that fail (286/286 agree).

**Results with this PR:**

| build | result |
|---|---|
| default `120a` configure, CUDA 13.0: `ninja cutlass_profiler` | **builds and links**: 1981 objects, 0 failures. The 350 library shards contain 500 SM120 blockscaled GEMMs (286 + 214 grouped), all `128x128x128` |
| default `120a` configure, CUDA 12.8: `ninja cutlass_profiler` | all 500 SM120 blockscaled GEMMs compile. 5 profiler/reference objects (`gemm_int4.cu`, `conv2d.cu`, `conv3d.cu`, `gemm_int8_interleaved_64.cu`, `device_allocation.cu`) still fail with `subbyte_reference.h(459): error: too few arguments in function call` (`__nv_atomic_load_n`). That is a separate CUDA 12.8 issue, fixed by #3301, and unrelated to this change |
| `CUTLASS_LIBRARY_KERNELS=cutlass3x_sm120_bstensorop_gemm*_128x{8,16,32,64}x*`, CUDA 12.8: every generated kernel | **1042 / 1042 compile** (597 non-grouped + 445 grouped) |

The generator has no unit-test harness in-tree, so I did not add a test.

Closes #3646

title: [CuTe DSL] Allow selected read-only inline_ptx operands to be materialized into a register
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/pull/3642/files) against `main`.

## Summary

`cute.arch.inline_ptx` lowers a compile-time constant read-only operand to the immediate constraint `n` regardless of what the target instruction accepts. Some PTX instructions take only a register in a given operand slot, so such a constant is rejected by ptxas. This adds `force_register_args`, an opt-in that names the read-only operands which must be moved into a register first.

Refs #3640.

## Minimal failure

```python
@cute.kernel
def kernel():
    value = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
    zero = Int32(0)
    cute.arch.inline_ptx(
        "max.xorsign.abs.bf16x2 {$w0}, {$r0}, {$r1};",
        write_only_types=[Int32],
        read_only_args=[zero, value],
    )
```

Generated PTX on an L20 (sm_89, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.dev0`):

```ptx
mov.u32 	%r3, %tid.x;
max.xorsign.abs.bf16x2 %r1, 0, %r2;      // immediate operand
```

```
ptxas application ptx input, line 32; error   : Arguments mismatch for instruction 'max'
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
```

## Where the constraint is chosen

Not in this repository. `NVVM_InlinePtxOp` carries no per-operand register request (only `readOnlyArgs`, `readWriteArgs`, `ptxCode`, `predicate`, `memoryClobber`). The constraint comes from the NVVM to LLVM conversion, `mlir/lib/Dialect/LLVMIR/IR/BasicPtxBuilderInterface.cpp`:

```cpp
static FailureOr<char> getRegisterType(Value v, Location loc) {
  if (v.getDefiningOp<LLVM::ConstantOp>())
    return 'n';
  return getRegisterType(v.getType(), loc);
}
```

The value-level overload returns `n` for any constant without consulting the instruction, so the generated `llvm.inline_asm` gets the constraint string `"=r,n,r"`.

## What this changes

`inline_ptx(..., force_register_args=(0,))` materializes the named read-only operands with an explicit `mov` before the target instruction runs:

```ptx
mov.b32 %r2, 0;
max.xorsign.abs.bf16x2 %r1, %r2, %r3;
```

which is the output #3640 asks for. The operand the target instruction sees is produced by an instruction rather than by a constant op, so the existing type-based register constraint applies. Nothing else changes: the default is `None`, unnamed operands keep today's behavior, and indices refer to `read_only_args` only — out-of-range, negative, bare-int and non-integer indices raise.

## Why not disable immediates globally

A constant is legal, and preferable, in plenty of operand slots (`add.s32`, `mbarrier.init.b64`, ...). Making `getRegisterType(Value)` return `r` for every constant would be a semantics change well beyond this issue. The opt-in is therefore per call site, and the existing immediate path is untouched — covered by `test_default_path_is_unchanged` and by the `add.s32` cases in the verification below.

## Verification

Hardware: 1× NVIDIA L20, compute capability 8.9, driver 570.86.10, `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_89`.
Environment: `nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.dev0` (cu12 libraries), PTX generated by CUDA 13.4.46 / NVVM 23.0.0. Baseline is `f614dc40e17fb3ddb1b7b474318b48a8d5d21a2c`.

End-to-end path (Python DSL → lowering → PTX → ptxas → launch → host readback), 32 lanes of packed bf16 covering ±0, ±1, ±2 and ±0.5, compared as raw bit patterns:

| Variant | Compile | Bit-exact readback |
|---|---|---|
| `Int32(0)` as reported | FAIL — `Arguments mismatch for instruction 'max'` | — |
| constant read from memory (pre-change workaround) | PASS | 32/32 |
| `llvm.inline_asm` with explicit `=r,r,r` | PASS | 32/32 |
| `force_register_args=(0,)` | PASS | 32/32 |

Regression matrix, all executed on the device: literal zero; non-zero and negative finite constants; a constant produced by folding; the constant in the second read-only position; two identical constants with only one opted in; a read-only placeholder repeated twice; dynamic operands with and without the opt-in; an instruction where an immediate is legal, with and without the opt-in; two write-only results with a forced constant; and the argument-validation cases. The new test file covers the same IR shapes on CPU, so it needs neither a GPU nor ptxas.

Timing was measured with CUDA events in an interleaved paired run (60 rounds memory-bound, 40 rounds register-resident) including an A/A arm that recompiles and re-measures the patched variant under a second label. The fixed kernel matches the existing workarounds within the A/A noise band (about ±1.2%); the materialized `mov` is hoisted out of the loop and absorbed by register allocation. This is a correctness change, not a throughput change.

Two failures observed while testing are **not** addressed here, and reproduce without this change: `inline_ptx(predicate=...)` emits `@0` instead of the predicate's operand index, and a float read-only constant fails with `constraint 'n' expects an integer constant expression`. Float operands are therefore rejected by `force_register_args` with an explicit error rather than silently ignored.

## Scope and open questions

This is a CUTLASS-side wrapper. The complete fix belongs in LLVM/MLIR — a per-operand register request on `NVVM_InlinePtxOp` honoured by `BasicPtxBuilderInterface` — which then has to reach a release wheel. This repository has no copy of that C++, and the wheel ships a statically linked compiler, so that path cannot be validated from here.

The parameter name is a proposal. Feedback on the name, on whether the `mov` materialization is the right shape, or on waiting for the compiler-side attribute instead, is welcome.

Not tested: sm_100 (the reported target; this host is sm_89), and NaN/subnormal bit-level semantics.

title: [examples/77] Order each load-warp lane's producer_acquire wait before the TMA it guards
body:
*Found by an ongoing project that formally verifies GPU kernels by checking their PTX against the PTX memory model.*

> **This is a proposed fix for a suspected bug, not a confirmed one.** We are opening it to ask whether the missing ordering is a real defect or something the code deliberately relies on. If it is the latter, please close this PR.

## Summary

In the SM100 FMHA load collectives, the whole load warp executes `producer_acquire` (an mbarrier parity wait), but only the elected lane issues the TMA:

```cpp
uint32_t lane_predicate = cute::elect_one_sync();
pipeline_q.producer_acquire(pipeline_q_producer_state);   // all 32 lanes: empty_barrier.wait(phase)
if (lane_predicate) {
  copy(params.tma_load_q.with(*tma_barrier, 0), ...);      // elected lane only
}
```

Under PTX's per-thread semantics, nothing orders a non-elected lane's wait before the elected lane's TMA. Suppose a non-elected lane reaches its wait only after the elected lane has issued the load and the consumer has released the buffer. Q is released once per tile, so by then the empty barrier has moved to its next phase. That lane is still waiting for parity 1, which will never come again, so the load warp hangs.

This PR adds a `__syncwarp()` after each `producer_acquire` in `sm100_fmha_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` and `sm100_fmha_mla_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`, 12 sites in total, with a comment explaining why.

## Where the race is

Time runs downwards. Lanes 0 and k are in the same load warp. Line numbers are from `f614dc40`: `load` is `examples/77_blackwell_fmha/collective/sm100_fmha_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`, `mainloop` is `sm100_fmha_fwd_mainloop_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`, `pipeline` is `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp`.

| # | Load warp, elected lane | Load warp, lane k | Consumer warps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `producer_acquire` for Q: waits parity 1 and returns, `load:242`, wait at `pipeline:1100` | **has not reached its wait yet** | blocked in `consumer_wait` |
| 2 | issues the TMA for Q, `load:245` | | |
| 3 | | | wait returns, reads Q |
| 4 | | | `consumer_release` for Q, `mainloop:474`, which flips the empty barrier to its next phase |
| 5 | | now reaches `producer_acquire` and waits for parity 1, `load:242` | |
| 6 | | **that phase is already gone, so the wait never returns** | |

Row 5 is the race, and row 6 is the hang. Parity 1 is the producer's initial phase, from `InitialProducerPhase` in `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:257`. Q is the dangerous buffer because it is released once per tile; the multi-stage K/V ring gives lanes more slack before the same thing happens.

## Is this a real bug?

This is a hazard in the PTX model that current ptxas does not expose:

- In the compiled fp16 fwd kernel, the elected-lane copy is emitted as an unconditional, uniform `UTMALDG`. There is no divergence between `producer_acquire` and the TMA, so all 32 lanes execute each wait together. In a reduced reproduction of about 200 million CTAs, all 32 lanes passed every wait in the same cycle.
- The failure mechanism itself is real. Forcing one lane to execute its parity-1 wait after the consumer's release hangs that lane every time. When the wait is placed in a genuinely divergent region, the hardware scheduler does let the non-elected lanes fall behind, and they hang on the multi-stage K/V ring.

So the code currently depends on ptxas proving that the warp is converged. The `__syncwarp()` makes that ordering explicit.

**The question we would like answered:** is this a real bug? Concretely, are the load collectives intended to rely on ptxas keeping the load warp converged across `producer_acquire` and the elected-lane TMA, so the lanes can never diverge? If that reliance is deliberate, we are happy to close this, especially given the MLA cost below. If it is incidental, this patch is the minimal fix and we can adjust it however you prefer.

## Cost

- **fwd kernel:** ptxas proves the warp convergent and emits no additional `WARPSYNC`; the binary is in fact slightly smaller.
- **MLA fwd kernel:** 144 additional `WARPSYNC.ALL` instructions across all instantiations.

## Testing

B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.2, driver 595.58.03, fp16, the example's compile flags.

- Upstream CMake test options pass, as on `main`: fmha 8 of 8, MLA fwd 5 of 5.

**Performance** (fp16, head dim 128 for fmha; latent 128 / rope 64 for MLA):

| Kernel and configuration | `main` | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fmha fwd, b=4 h=32 s=8192 | 916.7 TFLOPS | 915.7 TFLOPS | −0.1% |
| fmha fwd, same, causal | 766.0 TFLOPS | 769.2 TFLOPS | +0.4% |
| MLA fwd, b=4 h=16 s=4096 | 1059.1 TFLOPS | 1057.5 TFLOPS | −0.1% |
| MLA fwd, same, causal | 836.4 TFLOPS | 835.0 TFLOPS | −0.2% |

Median of three interleaved runs on an otherwise idle B200. The third repetition partly overlapped another user's job for the MLA, gen and example-93 rows; the median absorbs that one outlier. All differences are within run-to-run noise.

Co-written by Claude.

title: [examples/77] Wait for TMEM statistics stores before publishing them to the correction warpgroup
body:
*Found by an ongoing project that formally verifies GPU kernels by checking their PTX against the PTX memory model.*

> **This is a proposed fix for a suspected bug, not a confirmed one.** We are opening it to ask whether the missing ordering is a real defect or something the code deliberately relies on. If it is the latter, please close this PR.

## Summary

In the softmax path of the SM100 FMHA mainloops, the row statistics are written to TMEM and then published to the correction warpgroup:

```cpp
// softmax warpgroup
copy(tiled_tmem_storev, tTMEM_STOREVrS, tTMEM_STOREVtS);   // tcgen05.st (asynchronous)
pipeline_c.producer_commit(pipeline_c_producer_state);      // mbarrier.arrive

// correction warpgroup
pipeline_s0_c.consumer_wait(pipeline_s0_c_consumer_state);
copy(tiled_tmem_loadv, tTMEM_LOADVtS0, tTMEM_LOADVrS);      // tcgen05.ld of the same columns
```

There is no `tcgen05.wait::st` between the store and the arrive, so the notification is not ordered after the asynchronous TMEM write (PTX ISA §9.7.18.6.4.4). This occurs twice per mainloop:

1. the per-iteration old/new row max, published every KV tile, and
2. the final row max and row sum, published when `final_call` is set.

The same function already uses the correct idiom for the P matrix:

```cpp
copy(tiled_tmem_store, ...);
cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_tmem_store();   // tcgen05.wait::st
pipeline_s.consumer_release(pipeline_s_consumer_state);
```

This PR adds `cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_tmem_store()` after both statistics stores in the fwd, gen and MLA-fwd mainloops, six sites in total. Both call sites are warp-uniform, as the `.sync.aligned` wait requires.

## Where the race is

Time runs downwards, for the final statistics. Line numbers are from `f614dc40`, in `examples/77_blackwell_fmha/collective/sm100_fmha_fwd_mainloop_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`.

| # | Softmax warpgroup | TMEM store, in flight | Correction warpgroup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tcgen05.st` of row max and row sum, `:721` | accepted, **not yet visible** | blocked in `consumer_wait` |
| 2 | *(this PR inserts `tcgen05.wait::st` here)* | | |
| 3 | `producer_commit`, an `mbarrier.arrive`, `:780` | still in flight | |
| 4 | | still in flight | wait returns |
| 5 | | still in flight | `tcgen05.ld` of the same columns, `:1079` and `:1124` |
| 6 | | store lands | correction has already used the old values |

Row 5 is the race: the arrive at row 3 carries no guarantee that the store at row 1 is visible. The per-iteration row max has the same shape at `:611` and `:613`.

## Is this a real bug?

**The gap survives compilation.** `tcgen05.wait::st` is a real SASS instruction, `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.T`, and ptxas does not insert it on its own. In the fp16 `77_blackwell_fmha` binary built from `main`, every one of the 112 `STTM.x2` statistics stores reaches the following `SYNCS.ARRIVE` with no fence in between. With this PR all 112 are fenced; the `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.T` count goes from 120 to 232.

**We could not make it fail on B200.** We rebuilt the pattern in a small kernel: store, arrive, then load from the other warpgroup. It compared about 2.65 trillion loaded values against a stale pattern written beforehand. The detector was calibrated to catch a write landing 50 or more cycles after the arrive. No stale value appeared, including with a 1024-deep store backlog, extra warps streaming TMEM stores, and 4 KB stores. Timing `tcgen05.wait::st` in isolation shows the data becomes visible to another warp's `tcgen05.ld` before the store reports completion. The current code relies on that property, which is not documented.

**The question we would like answered:** is this a real bug? The PTX model appears to require the wait, and ptxas does not close the gap for you, so it is still there in the shipped binary. But we could not make it fail, which suggests the mainloop relies on TMEM stores becoming visible to another warpgroup's `tcgen05.ld` before `tcgen05.wait::st` reports completion. Is that ordering guaranteed by the hardware and intended to be relied on here? If so, we will close this. If not, this patch is the minimal fix and we can adjust it however you prefer.

## Testing

B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.2, driver 595.58.03, fp16, the examples' compile flags.

- Upstream CMake test options pass, as on `main`: fmha 8 of 8, fmha_gen 5 of 5, MLA fwd 5 of 5.

**Performance** (fp16, head dim 128 for fmha; latent 128 / rope 64 for MLA):

| Kernel and configuration | `main` | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fmha fwd, b=4 h=32 s=8192 | 916.7 TFLOPS | 919.3 TFLOPS | +0.3% |
| fmha fwd, same, causal | 766.0 TFLOPS | 773.1 TFLOPS | +0.9% |
| MLA fwd, b=4 h=16 s=4096 | 1059.1 TFLOPS | 1057.7 TFLOPS | −0.1% |
| MLA fwd, same, causal | 836.4 TFLOPS | 836.7 TFLOPS | +0.0% |
| fmha gen, b=64 h=32 h_k=8 k=8192 | 4.19 TB/s | 4.19 TB/s | 0.0% |

Median of three interleaved runs on an otherwise idle B200. The third repetition partly overlapped another user's job for the MLA, gen and example-93 rows; the median absorbs that one outlier. All differences are within run-to-run noise.

Co-written by Claude.

title: [examples/93] Wait for the Acc2 tcgen05.ld before releasing TMEM to the MMA warp
body:
*Found by an ongoing project that formally verifies GPU kernels by checking their PTX against the PTX memory model.*

> **This is a proposed fix for a suspected bug, not a confirmed one.** We are opening it to ask whether the missing ordering is a real defect or something the code deliberately relies on. If it is the latter, please close this PR.

## Summary

In `EPILOG_warp` (`examples/93_blackwell_low_latency_gqa/tgv_gqa.cuh`), the final Acc2 read is followed by the notification that lets the MMA warp free TMEM:

```cpp
tmem_load<decltype(bmm2_tmem_load)>(acc2_tmem_addr, tAcc2rAcc2);   // tcgen05.ld (asynchronous)
if (lane_id < (CTA_dH / NumEpilogWarps)) {
  // only these lanes consume tAcc2rAcc2 (st.async to the reduction CTA)
}
arrive_barrier(shared_storage.tmem_allocation_result_barrier);
```

and in the MMA warp:

```cpp
arrive_barrier(shared_storage.tmem_allocation_result_barrier);
wait_barrier(shared_storage.tmem_allocation_result_barrier, 1);
tmem_allocator.free(shared_storage.bmm1_tmem_base_ptr, Acc1_col_max);
tmem_allocator.free(shared_storage.bmm2_tmem_base_ptr, Acc2_col_max);
```

With the example's default `dH = 64` the condition is `lane_id < 16`, so lanes 16–31 of each epilogue warp never use their loaded registers. Nothing orders their `tcgen05.ld` before the arrive that allows the deallocation. PTX ISA §9.7.18.6.4.4 ("Non-pipelined instructions, different thread") requires `tcgen05.wait::ld` before synchronizing with another thread. §9.7.18.6.4.5 notes that a register dependency orders only the dependent instruction in the same thread, so even the consuming lanes are not formally covered.

This PR adds `cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_tmem_load()` (`tcgen05.wait::ld`) right after the load. That is the idiom this kernel already uses for Acc1 before it signals the next BMM1 (`tgv_gqa.cuh:1325`).

## Where the race is

Time runs downwards. Line numbers are from `f614dc40`. Both epilogue lanes below are in the same warp; the MMA warp is the TMEM owner.

| # | Epilogue lanes 0–15 | Epilogue lanes 16–31 | MMA warp (TMEM owner) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tcgen05.ld` Acc2 issued, `tgv_gqa.cuh:1514` | `tcgen05.ld` Acc2 issued, `:1514` | blocked in `wait_barrier`, `:882` |
| 2 | read the registers, `:1516`–`:1527` | **never read them**, so no dependency forces the load to finish | |
| 3 | `arrive_barrier`, `:1530` | `arrive_barrier`, `:1530` | |
| 4 | | | wait returns: all 160 arrivals in, `:882` |
| 5 | | **load may still be in flight** | `tmem_allocator.free`, `:885`–`:886` |
| 6 | | load completes against TMEM this CTA has already released | |

Row 5 is the race. This CTA never reuses those columns itself, since the scheduler is non-persistent and the CTA exits just after the free; the columns go back to the SM's allocator, which may hand them to another CTA, and the allocation lock is released early at `:819` precisely so that can happen. Note also that rows 1 to 2 do not save the consuming lanes: PTX ISA §9.7.18.6.4.5 says a register dependency orders only that instruction in that same thread, not another thread's view of the TMEM.

## Is this a real bug?

We could not produce a failure on hardware, and on CUDA 13.2 the change does not alter the generated code:

- ptxas already puts the `LDTM` scoreboard wait on the `lane_id < 16` branch, so the whole warp waits for the load before it diverges. Patched and unpatched `93_blackwell_low_latency_gqa` SASS differ only in `NOP` padding.
- A reduced reproduction of this barrier protocol on B200 ran about 14 billion CTAs, with and without `-Xptxas -g-tmem-access-check` and compute-sanitizer. It produced no guardrail trap, sanitizer error, or wrong value.

So the current code is safe because of how ptxas schedules this particular shape, not because the program orders it. The patch states the PTX-required ordering explicitly, and the generated code does not change.

**The question we would like answered:** is this a real bug? Concretely, is `EPILOG_warp` intended to rely on ptxas placing the `LDTM` scoreboard wait ahead of the `lane_id` branch, so that the non-consuming lanes' loads are complete before the arrive? If that reliance is deliberate and guaranteed, we are happy to close this. If it is incidental, this patch is the minimal fix and we can adjust it however you prefer.

## Testing

B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.2, driver 595.58.03, built with `nvcc -O3 -std=c++17 -gencode arch=compute_100a,code=sm_100a`.

- Builds cleanly. SASS is identical to `main` apart from `NOP` padding.
- Performance is identical by construction; measured numbers are below.

**Performance** (`93_blackwell_low_latency_gqa` defaults: kvH=8, qH=64, kvL=2048, dH=64; time per iteration):

| Configuration | `main` | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `--mode 0` (contiguous KV cache) | 4.91 µs | 4.91 µs | −0.1% |
| `--mode 1` (paged KV cache) | 5.25 µs | 5.26 µs | +0.1% |

Median of three interleaved runs on an otherwise idle B200. The third repetition partly overlapped another user's job; the median absorbs that one outlier.

Co-written by Claude.

title: Fix dilated Conv2d/Conv3d output size calculation
body:
## Summary

- compute Conv2d P/Q from the effective dilated filter extent, `(filter - 1) * dilation + 1`
- apply the same correction to Conv3d Z for both symmetric and asymmetric padding constructors
- add regression tests for dilated 2D/3D problems, asymmetric padding and stride, and 1x1 filters

## Background

The existing formula subtracts `filter * dilation`. It agrees with the standard convolution output-size formula only when dilation is 1. For dilation greater than 1 it undersizes the output, and a 1x1 filter is incorrectly made smaller by increasing dilation.

## Contribution roles

I led the contribution direction and acceptance criteria, reviewed and approved
the final design, and reviewed every changed line. I understand the change and
own the final design decision and the submission. AI assistance was used for
repository research, root-cause analysis, implementation preparation, and
automated validation execution.

## Testing

- reproduced the bug on the unmodified main branch: 2D output `3x4` instead of `4x6`, and 3D output `4x3x4` instead of `5x4x6`
- manually compiled and ran `test/unit/conv/problem_size.cpp` with MSVC 19.44, CUDA 12.9 headers, CCCL headers, and GoogleTest v1.14.0
- all 5 regression tests passed

Fixes #3502

title: Fix packed uint1b logical array reductions
body:
## Summary

- fix the `uint1b_t` logical OR reduction specialization to accept `logical_or`
- use the correct identities and packed-byte checks for logical AND and OR
- mask padding bits in partial trailing bytes
- add regression coverage across logical bit and storage boundaries

## Background

The logical OR specialization currently cannot be called through `ReduceArray` because its operator takes `logical_and`. Even when called directly through the specialization, its `true` identity makes an all-zero array reduce to true.

The logical AND specialization checks whether each storage byte is nonzero rather than whether every valid bit is set. For example, `0x7f` incorrectly reduces to true. Partial trailing bytes also need a mask so padding bits do not participate in either reduction.

This change keeps the packed-byte path: full bytes are reduced directly, while only the valid low bits of a partial trailing byte are considered.

## Contribution roles

I led the contribution direction and acceptance criteria, reviewed and approved
the final design, and reviewed every changed line. I understand the change and
own the final design decision and the submission. AI assistance was used for
repository research, root-cause analysis, implementation preparation, and
automated validation execution.

## Testing

- reproduced the public logical OR helper compilation failure on the unmodified main branch
- reproduced incorrect runtime results on main: AND of `[1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0]` returned 1, and OR of an all-zero array returned 1
- manually compiled and ran the new regression source with MSVC 19.44, CUDA 12.9 headers, CCCL headers, and GoogleTest v1.14.0
- 2/2 tests passed, exhaustively checking each logical position for `N = 1, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 32`, including padding-bit isolation
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #3510

title: [CuTeDSL] Add BF16 support to Hopper dense GEMM examples
body:
## Motivation

BF16 is the dominant dtype for LLM training and inference, and SM90 WGMMA supports it natively (`wgmma.mma_async ... .f32.bf16.bf16`). The CuTe DSL primitive already allows it: `warpgroup.MmaF16BF16Op` accepts `BFloat16` A/B with `Float32` accumulation. But the Hopper `dense_gemm.py` and `dense_gemm_persistent.py` examples rejected BF16 in `is_valid_dtypes`, so the most common Hopper GEMM configuration could not be run with the reference examples. The Blackwell dense GEMM examples already support BF16.

## Modifications

- `dense_gemm.py`, `dense_gemm_persistent.py`:
  - Allow `BFloat16` A/B, with `Float32` accumulation only. This matches the WGMMA / `MmaF16BF16Op` constraint. `BFloat16` with `Float16` accumulation is still rejected.
  - Allow `BFloat16` output with `Float32` accumulation.
  - Update the module/class docstrings (supported types, accumulator rules, alignment) and the stale `TypeError` messages.
- New `test/examples/CuTeDSL/hopper/test_dense_gemm.py`. Neither kernel had tests before. It uses the existing L0/L1 structure and covers both kernels × {Float16, BFloat16}:
  - L0 compile: all tile shapes (128x256, 128x128, 128x64, 64x64)
  - L1 correctness against `torch.einsum`: tile shapes, cluster shapes (1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, including multicast), all 8 A/B/C major combinations (batched, L=2), output dtypes {F16, BF16, F32}, non-tile-aligned sizes (1000x1032x264, 136x72x72x3)
  - Validation: BF16 + F32 acc accepted; BF16 + F16 acc and mixed BF16/F16 rejected

The kernel code itself is not changed. BF16 uses the same code path as FP16, and only the operand type of the MMA/TMA atoms differs.

## Correctness

NVIDIA H200 (SM90a), driver 580.159.03, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0.dev0`, torch 2.14.0+cu130:

```
$ cd test/examples/CuTeDSL
$ pytest hopper/test_dense_gemm.py -q --target-cc 90 --test-level L2
102 passed in 127.16s
```

Regression check: FP8 (E4M3FN → F16) and INT8 (→ Int32) still PASS on both modified kernels.

SASS check (`CUTE_DSL_KEEP=cubin`, `cuobjdump -sass`, tile 128x256):

| | PTX | SASS | # MMA | # TMA/SYNCS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP16 | `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64n256k16.f32.f16.f16` | `HGMMA.64x256x16.F32` | 8 | 38 |
| BF16 | `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64n256k16.f32.bf16.bf16` | `HGMMA.64x256x16.F32.BF16` | 8 | 38 |

## Performance

H200, A/B/C K-major/K-major/N-major, F32 accumulation, tile 128x256, cluster 1x1, hot L2, 10 warmup + 50 timed iterations. cuBLAS is `torch.matmul` (BF16) on the same shape. Units are TFLOP/s.

`dense_gemm_persistent.py`:

| M, N, K | DSL FP16 | DSL BF16 | cuBLAS BF16 | DSL BF16 / cuBLAS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096, 4096, 4096 | 866.3 | 865.8 | 800.5 | 1.08x |
| 8192, 8192, 8192 | 827.7 | 836.6 | 748.3 | 1.12x |
| 4096, 14336, 4096 | 891.0 | 892.5 | 789.8 | 1.13x |
| 4096, 4096, 14336 | 921.9 | 919.4 | 806.0 | 1.14x |
| 16384, 8192, 1024 | 793.9 | 788.8 | 732.3 | 1.08x |
| 8192, 4096, 512 | 638.0 | 636.8 | 627.7 | 1.01x |

BF16 performance matches FP16 within run-to-run noise (about ±2%), as expected because BF16 and FP16 WGMMA have the same throughput. The non-persistent `dense_gemm.py` reaches 815–905 TFLOP/s on the square/LLM shapes (1.04–1.11x cuBLAS) and 0.96x cuBLAS on the short-K 16384x8192x1024 shape, where per-tile prologue/epilogue is not amortized.

## Testing notes

To run the public example tests outside NVIDIA CI I needed `--target-cc 90`, because `test/utils/test_sharding.py` otherwise imports `device_info`, which is not in the repository. I also needed `pytest<9`, because the plugin imports `_pytest.assertion.util.running_on_ci`. These are unrelated to this PR.

title: [CuTe] Reject Copy_Atom copies whose src/dst size does not match the CopyOp (#3488)
body:
## Motivation

#3488: `copy_if(Copy_Atom<...>, prd, src, dst)` with a smaller `dst` silently writes out of bounds. I reproduced it host-only with g++ 13 and ASan, using the issue's example (`UniversalCopy<uint128_t>` over `float`, `src` (4,3), `dst` (2,3)):

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 16
    #3 cute::copy_unpack<...>        include/cute/atom/copy_traits.hpp:133
    #4 cute::Copy_Atom<...>::call    include/cute/atom/copy_atom.hpp:149
```

One correction to the issue: the sibling `copy(Copy_Atom<...>{}, src, dst)` is **not** safe either. The same repro through `copy` gives the same 16-byte out-of-bounds write (`copy_atom.hpp:103`). Only the atom-less `copy(src, dst)` avoids the instruction.

## Root cause

`Copy_Atom::call()` dispatches to `copy_unpack()` as soon as **either** slice has the instruction's element count (`is_constant<NumValSrc, size(src)> || is_constant<NumValDst, size(dst)>`). `copy_unpack()` then recasts both slices to the CopyOp's register type and only checks the **register count**:

```cpp
Tensor rD = recast<RegTypeDst>(dst);
CUTE_STATIC_ASSERT_V(size(rD) == Int<RegNumDst>{}, ...);
```

`recast<>` rounds a partial register up to a whole one. A 2-float (64-bit) slice recast to `uint128_t` therefore still has size 1, the assertion passes, and the 128-bit instruction writes past the slice.

## Modifications

- `include/cute/atom/copy_traits.hpp`: the generic `copy_unpack()` now also requires that `src` and `dst` hold **exactly** as many bits as the CopyOp's registers (`size(t) * sizeof_bits_v<value_type> == RegNum * sizeof_bits_v<RegType>`). The check is done per side, so converting ops whose src and dst registers differ are unaffected. A mismatch now fails to compile:
  ```
  error: static assertion failed: Copy_Traits: dst tensor size does not match this CopyOp.
         The copy would access memory outside the dst tensor.
  ```
  The `copy_unpack` overloads for the SM80/SM90/SM100 TMA, im2col and async ops are not changed.
- `include/cute/algorithm/copy.hpp`: the elementwise `copy_if(pred, src, dst)` loops over `size(dst)` while indexing `pred` and `src`. It now statically rejects `src`/`dst` of different static sizes. Dynamic sizes are left alone, because there is no device-side error channel.
- `test/unit/cute/core/tensor_algs.cpp`: host tests for `copy(Copy_Atom)`, `copy_if(Copy_Atom)` with one rest-slice masked off, and the elementwise `copy_if`. The rejection itself is a `static_assert` in a function body, so it cannot be a runtime or SFINAE test. It is shown by the repro below.

## Testing

Host repro from the issue, g++ 13.3 + ASan:

| | `copy_if(Copy_Atom)` | `copy(Copy_Atom)` | correctly sized (4,3)→(4,3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | OOB write (ASan) | OOB write (ASan) | OK |
| after | **compile error** (message above) | **compile error** | OK, ASan clean, values correct |

This is a compile-time check in CuTe core, so I also confirmed that it does not reject any in-tree use. CUDA 12.8, `-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS="80;90a;100a"`. Everything below compiles with the new asserts and passes on NVIDIA A800 (SM80) and H200 (SM90):

| target | result |
|---|---|
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_core` (includes the 3 new tests) | 51 passed |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_layout` / `_turing` | 4 / 3 passed |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_ampere` | 228 passed (A800 and H200) |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_ampere_tiled_cp_async` | 4 passed (A800 and H200) |
| `cutlass_test_unit_cute_hopper_{stsm, bulk_load, bulk_store, tma_load, tma_store, cooperative_gemm}` | 1 / 3 / 3 / 9 / 7 / 1 passed (H200) |
| `cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_tensorop_f32_sm80_3x` (3.x collective GEMM) | 10 passed (A800 and H200) |
| `cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_tensorop_cluster_multicast_sm90` | 92 passed (H200) |
| `cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_tensorop_gmma_rs_warpspecialized_sm90` | 16 passed (H200) |

**SM100 (compile-only; I have no SM100 hardware).** *Correction:* an earlier version of this description said the Blackwell tests were compiled, but `test/unit/cute` has no SM100-specific tests, so that claim was wrong. I then compiled these SM100 GEMM targets with the new asserts (CUDA 12.8, `100a`): `cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_tensorop_sm100_f16xf16`, `_tensorop_sm100_f8xf8`, and `_bstensorop_sm100_nvf4xnvf4`. They cover the TMEM-load epilogues, TMA stores and the UTCCP scale-factor copies.

- **9 of 13 objects compile, and the new asserts do not fire in any of them.**
- **4 objects fail with `include/cutlass/subbyte_reference.h(459): error: too few arguments in function call`** (`__nv_atomic_load_n` under CUDA 12.8). This is unrelated to this PR. I compiled one of the failing objects (`f16_f16_f16_f16_fusion.cu`) with `main`'s unmodified CuTe headers and got the same error. It is addressed by #3301.

The TMA, TMEM (load/store/UTCCP) and im2col copies have their own `copy_unpack` overloads, so they do not go through the changed generic function. That includes the new SM107 collectives. I could not compile SM107 (it needs CUDA 13.4).

Not covered: `cutlass_test_unit_cute_volta` contains 0 tests for these architectures. I did not build `cutlass_profiler` or the full kernel library.

## Performance

None. The changes are `static_assert`s only, and no code generation changes.

Closes #3488

title: v4.8 update
[CuTeDSL] Make autotuning more user friendly & new docs
body:
This PR adds a lot of things to the overall CuTeDSL autotuning process to make it easier to use and more convenient:

- Add `derived_params` to autotuning API so it computes derived arguments that must be decided during compile time but rely on autotuned parameters (whose values are different per configuration tuned)
- Make `testing.autotune_jit` able to decorate a class. This is for people who prefer to implement kernels as classes that fix the compile time params in `__init__` method and pass runtime params to `__call__`, so now they can do this
```
@testing.autotune_jit(
    params_dict={"COPY_BITS": [32, 64, 128], "THREADS_M": [4, 8]},
    update_on_change=["M", "N"],
    warmup_iterations=10,
    iterations=50,
)
class ElementwiseAddKernel:
    THREADS_M = 4

    def __init__(self, COPY_BITS=128):
        self.COPY_BITS = COPY_BITS

    @cute.jit
    def __call__(self, mA, mB, mC, M, N):
        elementwise_add(
            mA, mB, mC, M, N,
            copy_bits=self.COPY_BITS,
            threads_m=self.THREADS_M,
        )
```
- Support pruning undesired configurations (either invalid or known to be suboptimal) -- this aligns with triton's `prune_configs_by` in their autotuning API
- Add `autotune_suite` API so now user can provide a list of representative shapes and find the best overall kernel candidates with the ranking rule: sort according to how many times a configuration is accepted across all inputs, where "accepted" mean for a input case the configuration is in the top `accept_percentile` fastest ones
- Better autotuning docs. Previously the doc only explains how to autotune manually which is quite painful at least for me

title: [C++] Fix EpilogueDirectStore warp index decomposition; reject sliced-K (#3496)
body:
## Motivation

#3496: `EpilogueDirectStore` computes the warp's (m, n) position in the threadblock tile with

```cpp
int warp_id_mn = warp_idx % (WarpCount::kM * WarpShape::kN);   // WarpShape::kN is the warp tile's N extent
```

`EpilogueBase` uses `WarpCount::kM * WarpCount::kN`, the number of warps in the MN plane.

I tried to build a failing config for the case described in the issue, `WarpCount::kN > WarpShape::kN`, and could not make a valid one. An 8-wide warp tile (for example 128x128x32 CTA with 128x8x32 warps) also fails with the **default** epilogue, so that config is not supported by the SM80 mainloop/epilogue in general. An N=16 warp tile would need at least 17 warps along N, which exceeds the register file. So that path is latent, as the issue says.

The typo **is** reachable through sliced-K (`kPartitionsK > 1`), which `EpilogueDirectStore` does not reject. For a 64x64x64 threadblock with 64x64x32 warps, WarpCount = (1, 1, 2). The second K-partition warp gets `warp_id_mn = 1 % (1 * 64) = 1`, so `warp_n = 1`, and it stores its partial sums into columns 64..127, the **neighbouring threadblock's output tile**. Those writes stay inside D, so compute-sanitizer reports nothing and the results are silently wrong. Even with the correct modulo, sliced-K cannot work with this epilogue: it stores accumulators straight from registers and has no cross-warp reduction over K partitions, so both K-partition warps would write different partial sums to the same elements.

## Modifications

`include/cutlass/epilogue/threadblock/epilogue_direct_store.h`:
- Use `WarpCount::kM * WarpCount::kN` for the MN-plane warp decomposition, matching `EpilogueBase`.
- Add `static_assert(kPartitionsK == 1, ...)` so that sliced-K configurations fail at compile time with a clear message, instead of producing wrong results.

## Testing

Built with CUDA 12.8, `-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS="80;90"`; run on NVIDIA H200 (SM90) and A800 (SM80).

- Existing test `SM80_Device_GemmUniversal_DirectStore_f16n_f16t_f32n_tensor_op_f32.128x128x32_64x64x32` (`cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_tensorop_f32_sm80`): **passes** on both GPUs with this change.
- Sliced-K diagnostic (not included in the PR): 64x64x64 threadblock / 64x64x32 warps / `DefaultEpilogueDirectStore`, run through `TestAllGemmUniversal`:
  - Same mainloop with the default epilogue: passes.
  - Direct store, original header: **fails** (memcheck: 0 errors, i.e. wrong values written inside D).
  - Direct store, modulo fix only: **fails** (no K-partition reduction).
  - Direct store, this PR: **compile error**:
    ```
    epilogue_direct_store.h(145): error: static assertion failed with "The direct store epilogue does not reduce
    accumulators across K partitions (sliced-K). Use a warp shape whose K extent equals the threadblock shape's K extent."
    ```

I did not add a runtime test for the `WarpCount::kN > WarpShape::kN` case, because I could not construct a supported configuration that reaches it (see above).

Closes #3496

title: [C++] Fix Stream-K broadcast epilogue reduction; document broadcast vector convention (#3540)
body:
## Motivation

#3540 reports that the ColumnMajor-output specializations of `GemmUniversalWithBroadcast` / `GemmUniversalStreamkWithBroadcast` misindex the broadcast vector. I added the missing test coverage for the vector under both output layouts and found two things:

1. **The ColumnMajor behavior is self-consistent, but it was not documented.** The specialization transposes the problem, so the underlying row-major kernel broadcasts `V` along *its* columns, which are the **rows** of the column-major `D`. The vector therefore has **M** elements, and the epilogue bounds-checks against M. With a length-M vector, results are correct and memcheck is clean. The OOB reads described in the issue only happen when a caller assumes a length-N vector. Rejecting `ptr_Vector` or changing the indexing would break callers that already use the length-M convention. A per-column vector for column-major D is also not expressible with this epilogue. So this PR takes the issue's other suggestion and **documents the convention**.
2. **A real bug in `GemmUniversalStreamkWithBroadcast`, independent of layout.** It produces wrong results whenever Stream-K splits the K loop across thread blocks, including plain RowMajor output with the default `LinearCombinationBiasElementwise` op. There was no in-tree test of this class.

## Root cause (Stream-K)

In separate-reduction mode, each block reduces one accumulator fragment `reduce_fragment_idx` of an output tile, and then `EpilogueStreamkWithBroadcast::reduce()` calls `EpilogueWithBroadcast::reduce()`. The single-source overload of that function stored the fragment through `destination_iterator` / `tensor_iterator` without advancing them to `reduce_fragment_idx`:

```cpp
destination_iterator.store(frag_Z);   // always fragment 0
++destination_iterator;
```

As a result, every fragment was written over fragment 0: most of D and T were never written, and fragment 0 got whichever peer wrote last. The source iterator *was* advanced (`source_iterator += reduce_fragment_idx`), so C was read from the right place. The dual-source overload in the same file and `Epilogue::reduce()` both do `iterator += reduce_fragment_idx` before storing. This PR makes the single-source overload match them. The function is only reached through `EpilogueStreamkWithBroadcast`.

## Modifications

- `epilogue_with_broadcast.h`: advance `destination_iterator` / `tensor_iterator` by `reduce_fragment_idx` before storing in the single-source `reduce()`.
- `gemm_universal_with_broadcast.h`, `gemm_universal_streamk_with_broadcast.h`: document how the vector is indexed. It always runs along the contiguous dimension of D: N elements for RowMajor, M elements for ColumnMajor. Also document what `ldr` / `batch_stride_Vector` mean, explain why the ColumnMajor specialization uses M, and complete the truncated "Supports" doc comment.
- New `test/unit/gemm/device/gemm_universal_with_broadcast_vector_sm80.cu` (added to `cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_broadcast`):
  - Inputs are small integers, so the half-precision results must match the reference **bit-exactly**, and every element of both **D (Z)** and **T** (`ptr_Tensor`) is checked.
  - The vector is allocated with exactly its documented length, so compute-sanitizer flags any overread.
  - Covers `GemmUniversalWithBroadcast` × {RowMajor, ColumnMajor} × {M>N, M<N, batched L=2 with `batch_stride_Vector`}, and `GemmUniversalStreamkWithBroadcast` × {RowMajor, ColumnMajor} × {unsplit K=64, Stream-K split K=512 and 520x392x1024, data-parallel `avail_sms=1`}.

## Correctness

Built with CUDA 12.8, `-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS="80;90"`; run on NVIDIA H200 (SM90) and A800 (SM80).

Before the fix (new test, unmodified headers):
```
[       OK ] SM80_Device_GemmWithBroadcast_f16t_f16n_f16t_tensor_op_f16.128x128_32x3_64x64x32_16x8x16
[       OK ] SM80_Device_GemmUniversalWithBroadcast_f16t_f16n_f16t_tensor_op_f32.vector_per_column
[       OK ] SM80_Device_GemmUniversalWithBroadcast_f16t_f16n_f16n_tensor_op_f32.vector_per_row
[  FAILED  ] SM80_Device_GemmUniversalStreamkWithBroadcast_f16t_f16n_f16t_tensor_op_f32.vector_per_column
             (32981 / 35904 mismatches at 136x264x512; 197730 / 203840 at 520x392x1024)
[  FAILED  ] SM80_Device_GemmUniversalStreamkWithBroadcast_f16t_f16n_f16n_tensor_op_f32.vector_per_row
```
The Stream-K cases pass with `avail_sms=1` (no peer reduction) and with K=64 (no split), which isolates the failure to the peer-reduction path.

After the fix:
```
$ ./test/unit/gemm/device/cutlass_test_unit_gemm_device_broadcast
[  PASSED  ] 5 tests.                                   # H200 and A800
$ compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck ... --gtest_filter='*vector_per*'
[  PASSED  ] 4 tests.
========= ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors                       # H200 and A800
$ ... --gtest_filter='*Streamk*' --gtest_repeat=50
50 / 50 iterations passed                               # A800
```

## Performance

No performance impact. The fix adds one iterator offset per reduced fragment in the Stream-K separate-reduction path, and the documentation changes are comments only.

Closes #3540

title: [CuTe DSL] Fix cross-CTA barrier scope and missing SFB wait in 2cta_mma_blockscale_m128 example, issue #3643
body:
## Problem (#3643)

`examples/python/CuTeDSL/experimental/primitives/tcgen05/2cta_mma_blockscale_m128.py` produces wrong results for larger problem sizes and hits `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED` for larger K. Reproduced on B200 (sm_100, CUDA 13.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with the reporter's `check_blockscale_sync.py`: 29/200 iterations mismatch at 4096x256x2048, launch failure at 8192x256x4096. `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` on the unmodified example reports `Barrier error detected. Missing wait` from the SFB TMA warp in the non-leader CTA on `sfb_smem_full`.

## Root cause

1. **The peer CTA's SFB completion is never observed.** Each CTA loads its own SFB half with a `cta_group::1` TMA tracked by its *local* `sfb_smem_full`. Only the leader's MMA warp waits, and only on the *leader's* barrier, before issuing the `cta_group::2` UTCCP that also reads the peer's sSFB. There is no path from the peer's `sfb_smem_full` to the leader.

2. **Cross-CTA arrives use `MemScope.CTA`.** `mbarrier_arrive(remote, scope=CTA)` lowers to `mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.shared::cluster.b64`, so the peer's SFA `cp.async` writes are not released at cluster scope before the leader's UTCCP reads them. (The default for a shared::cluster address is already `.cluster`; the example explicitly downgraded it.)

3. **No cross-proxy fence.** SFA is written through the generic proxy (`cp.async`) and read through the async proxy (`tcgen05.cp`).

## Fix

- Warp 7 (sync relay) also waits on `sfb_smem_full[stage]` before arriving on the leader's `ab_full[stage]`.
- Both cross-CTA `mbarrier_arrive` calls (the `ab_full` relay and the `tmem_dealloc` handshake) use `MemScope.CLUSTER`.
- `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` after the `a_local` wait, before the relay arrive.
- Updated the warp-7 comment, which said SFB "does not participate here".

## Verification (B200)

Using the reproducer from #3643 (`--repeats 300` per shape):

| variant | 4096x256x2048 | 8192x256x4096 | 16384x256x8192 |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream main | 29/200 FAIL | launch failure | — |
| only `ab_full` relay arrive → CLUSTER | 0/300 | — | — |
| only `tmem_dealloc` arrive → CLUSTER | 11/300 FAIL | — | — |
| only SFB wait added | 0/300 | 0/300 | 0/300 |
| this PR | 0/300 | 0/300 | 0/300 |

`compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` on this PR: 0 errors (8 before). The example's own `python 2cta_mma_blockscale_m128.py` and `--mnk 4096,256,2048` runs pass.

Isolating the two scope changes shows the `ab_full` relay arrive is what removes the mismatches on B200; adding only the SFB wait also passes here, but that is timing (SFB is small and normally lands before A/B), and synccheck still needs the wait to go clean. All three changes are kept.

Fixes #3643


title: [CuTe DSL] Preserve runtime tensor strides in Blackwell FMHA
body:
## Summary

Blackwell CuTe DSL FMHA accepts dynamic-layout Q/K/V/O/LSE tensors, but rebuilt its internal layouts from problem sizes using packed strides. Because the original iterators were paired with these synthesized layouts, padded tensor views could be addressed as if they were contiguous and silently produce incorrect results.

This change:

- maps the internal Q/K/V/O/LSE layouts from each input tensor runtime stride;
- preserves the intentional zero batch stride for varlen inputs, whose batch offsets come from cumulative sequence lengths; and
- corrects the LSE shape comment to match the actual allocation.

## Validation

- Python syntax check for fmha.py.
- NVIDIA GB200, CUDA 13.3, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.0: contiguous FP16 FMHA compilation and reference check passed.
- NVIDIA GB200: a local padded-stride case with B=2, GQA (8 query heads / 2 KV heads), and LSE enabled compiled and passed the reference check.

title: fix: handle ComposedLayout slicing with dynamic strides (fixes #3255)
body:
When slicing a Tensor whose layout is a ComposedLayout (e.g., Swizzle composed with a dynamic outer Layout), _cute_ir.slice fails because the Swizzle composition requires static stride analysis that cannot be performed with runtime dynamic strides (represented as '?' / unknown values).

The fix intercepts this case in _Tensor.__getitem__ and decomposes the ComposedLayout manually in the Python DSL layer:
1. Extract inner (Swizzle), offset, and outer (Layout) from the ComposedLayout
2. Slice only the outer Layout using slice_ (pure Layout slicing works with dynamic strides)
3. Compute the offset delta via crd2idx(coord_with_none_as_zero, outer)
4. Rebuild the ComposedLayout with the new offset and sliced outer
5. Construct a new Tensor with the original iterator

This avoids passing the composed layout with dynamic strides to the MLIR slice operation, which triggers an MLIR verifier error and segfault.

title: [SM90] Support MXFP4A8 Group Gemm for the SM90 mixed-input.
body:
Since the SM90 devices gained support for the int4 * fp8 computation pipeline, it has been widely adopted in inference frameworks such as SGLang and vLLM and delivered remarkable performance. 

However, with the evolution of large‑language models (LLMs), an increasing number of models employ higher‑precision parameters like MXFP4. Unfortunately, a large number of SM90 devices lack native support for this data type. Similar to the earlier int4 scenario, runtime dequantization is required for adaptation. Most existing schemes dequantize weights to BF16 for inference, which covers the vast majority of use cases. Nevertheless, this is clearly a fallback solution for SM90‑class devices that natively support FP8 GEMM operations. 

Accordingly, I have implemented the MXFP4‑to‑FP8 GEMM pipeline. Building upon existing work on WINT4A8, I realized dynamic scale retrieval and the corresponding GEMM computation logic, and removed the traditional fixed‑block‑size‑128 limitation of INT4A8. The implementation has been validated on SGLang. Results show that WMXFP4A8 outperforms existing pipelines in most scenarios.

## Summary

This PR adds MXFP4A8 activation block scaling support to the SM90 mixed-input ptr-array mainloop while preserving the existing int4a8 execution path.

The implementation gates the new activation-scale TMA, shared memory, and chunked accumulation logic behind the MXFP4A8-specific `EnableActBlockScale` condition. Non-MXFP4A8 paths, including int4a8, keep the original mainloop behavior.

## Changes

- Added activation block scale TMA descriptor, shared storage, and load path for MXFP4A8.
- Added chunked accumulation with activation scale application for MXFP4A8.
- Preserved the original `mma()` mainloop for non-act-block-scale paths.
- Added E2M1 to E4M3 numeric conversion coverage.
- Added static tests for int4a8 and MXFP4A8 path separation.

## Validation

Tested on machine H20 / SM90, CUDA `12.4.131`.

### Unit tests

